continuation_reasoning:
100 lockers, all closed initially. then 100 students pass by. each student toggles certain lockers. student 1 opens every locker, student 2 toggles every 2nd, student 3 every 3rd, and so on up to student 100. the question is which lockers are open at the end.

so, first, i need to figure out how many times each locker is toggled. because each time a locker is toggled, it switches from closed to open or open to closed. starting all closed, so if a locker is toggled an odd number of times, it will end up open; even number of times, closed.

so, for any given locker number n, how many times is it toggled? well, student k toggles locker n if k divides n. because student k toggles every k-th locker. so the number of times locker n is toggled is equal to the number of divisors of n.

for example, locker 6 is toggled by students 1, 2, 3, 6. so 4 times. since 4 is even, it ends up closed. but if a locker has an odd number of divisors, it will be open. but wait, normally numbers have divisors in pairs, like 6: 1 and 6, 2 and 3. so unless the number is a perfect square, where one divisor is repeated (sqrt(n)), otherwise divisors come in pairs. so perfect squares have an odd number of divisors because one divisor is repeated (sqrt(n)), so the count is odd.

so lockers that are perfect squares will be toggled an odd number of times and remain open. others will be toggled even times and remain closed. therefore, the open lockers are those whose numbers are perfect squares.

so in 100 lockers, the perfect squares are 1^2=1, 2^2=4, 3^2=9,... up to 10^2=100. so lockers 1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100 are open.

i think that's the answer. let me check with small numbers. say 10 lockers. perfect squares up to 10 are 1,4,9. so those should be open. let's simulate:

start: all closed.

student 1 opens all lockers. now all open.

student 2 toggles 2,4,6,8,10. so lockers 2,4,6,8,10 are closed now.

student 3 toggles 3,6,9. locker 3 closed, 6 closed (was open?), wait wait. initial state: after student 1, all open. student 2 toggles every 2nd: lockers 2,4,6,8,10 closed. student 3 toggles 3,6,9. locker 3 was open, now closed. locker 6 was closed, now open. locker 9 was open, now closed.

student 4 toggles 4,8. locker 4 was closed, now open. locker 8 closed, now open.

student 5 toggles 5,10. locker 5 was open, now closed. locker 10 closed, now open.

student 6 toggles 6,12 (but 12 is beyond 10). locker 6 was open, now closed.

student 7 toggles 7. locker 7 was open, now closed.

student 8 toggles 8. locker 8 was open, now closed.

student 9 toggles 9. locker 9 was closed, now open.

student 10 toggles 10. locker 10 was open, now closed.

so after all students, the open lockers are 1, 4, 9. which are the perfect squares. that matches. so the reasoning holds here.

so applying the same logic to 100 lockers, the perfect squares between 1 and 100 are the ones open. those are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100. total of 10 lockers.
